title: Long-form episode shot list
description: One file per episode: episode metadata + fact sources + voice config + the shot-by-shot render plan. Field naming rhymes with action-sequence-pipeline/specs/*.json (flat top-level object, snake_case, an 'id' field, nested objects for grouped config, lowercase free-text 'status' values tracked by the pipeline rather than by this schema's enum alone). See action-sequence-pipeline/specs/20260628_vesta_tfclose_chain_001.json for the sibling convention this schema mirrors. $comment blocks throughout mark rules JSON Schema cannot express (cross-field/cross-item comparisons, cross-object lookups) — those are enforced by validate_shotlist.py, not by a generic JSON Schema validator.

id.description: e.g. ep001_toilet_paper_tariff. Doubles as the base filename under pipeline/episodes/.

premise_id.description: Pointer back to the research doc / ideation-pull entry this episode came from, e.g. '14_live_ideation_pull_week_2026-08-24#toilet-paper-tariff'.

trigger_signal.description: The news/price/trend event that made this episode timely right now.

thesis.description: One-sentence claim the episode proves (the thing every shot should serve).

target_duration_s.description: Planned runtime in seconds. validate_shotlist.py checks actual shots[] duration against this within 10%.

status.description: Episode-level pipeline stage. 'verified' means every [VERIFY] claim below has a verified:true source; 'approved' is the fact-check + QA gate before render is final-packaged.

sources.description: Fact-check bibliography for this episode. Every shots[].verify_refs entry must resolve to a source.id here (checked by validate_shotlist.py, not expressible in JSON Schema).

shots.$comment: Ordering (ascending t_start_s), non-overlap, and total-duration-vs-target_duration_s are cross-item/cross-field rules JSON Schema's array/item validation cannot express against sibling items or against target_duration_s above. Enforced by validate_shotlist.py.

url.description: Primary-source URL (federal register notice, SEC filing, HTS schedule page, etc.). May be a placeholder/TBD URL while the source is an unverified stub.

quote.description: The exact quoted/extracted text that supports the claim. Empty string is allowed for a stub source not yet pulled.

claim_it_supports.description: Plain-language statement of what this source is being used to prove, so a reviewer doesn't have to reverse-engineer it from the shot list.

verified.description: true only once a human/process has actually opened the URL and confirmed the quote. False = stub, i.e. 'still needs verification'.

verified_date.description: Required once verified is true (see the sibling if/then below).

engine.description: The three Test-A candidates in research note 19 (private). Extend the enum here when a new engine is adopted.

voice_id.description: Engine-specific voice/clone identifier (ElevenLabs voice_id, Chatterbox reference-clip name, minted seed-audio voice tag).

script_path.description: Path to the clean VO script text actually fed to the engine (concatenation of shots[].script_line in order, or the file that generated them).

asset_type.description: chart=matplotlib/ffmpeg house style; ledger=the recurring Ledger template; card=ffmpeg drawtext template; still=nano-banana(+Ken Burns); clip_h3=local H3 t2v/i2v, 2 takes overnight; clip_hailuo=Hailuo browser workflow (action-sequence-pipeline generate_hailuo.js CDP driver); clip_seedance=Atlas Seedance 2.0, 1 take; archival=public-domain/licensed photo or footage; screencap=real document screen-capture (no generation).

shot_id.description: e.g. s01..s16. Unique within the episode (checked by validate_shotlist.py).

act.description: 1-based act number (Act 1 = the hook, Act 2 = the number, Act 3 = the cost stack, ... per doc 17's structure).

t_end_s.$comment: t_end_s > t_start_s cannot be expressed in JSON Schema (no same-object cross-field comparison keyword in 2020-12 without a $data extension). Enforced by validate_shotlist.py, along with cross-shot ordering/overlap.

script_line.description: The spoken VO for this shot. If this contains a factual number (digits, percent, cents, or number-words like 'thirds'/'nickel'/'dozen'/'half'), verify_refs is required and non-empty — see the if/then below and validate_shotlist.py's fuller NUMBER_RE heuristic.

on_screen.description: What's visible: composition, motion, on-screen text/graphics.

tool_params.description: Free-form per-asset_type generation parameters (e.g. for clip_seedance: {prompt, duration_s, resolution}; for chart: {chart_fn, data}; for still: {prompt, ref_style_board}). Intentionally unstructured here — each asset_type owns its own param shape in its generator script, the way action-sequence-pipeline specs vary opponent/environment/palette shape per fight_style.

takes.description: How many candidate generations to produce for picking (2 for H3 per doc 17's overnight-queue convention, 1 for Seedance, 1 for templated/code assets).

fallback_asset_type.description: What to fall back to if the primary generation fails/looks bad (e.g. clip_h3 -> still with Ken Burns, per research note 19 (private)'s Test B fallback rule).

verify_refs.description: source.id values from the episode's sources[] that back the factual number(s) in script_line. Must be non-empty when script_line contains a factual number (if/then below); each id must resolve to an existing, verified:true source before the episode can leave 'draft' status — both the existence check and the verified:true check are cross-object lookups that JSON Schema cannot express and that validate_shotlist.py performs instead.

asset_path.description: Filesystem/URL path to the picked render, once one exists. null while status is todo/generating.

status.description: todo=not started; generating=job submitted/queued; generated=take(s) exist, unpicked; picked=a take was chosen and asset_path is set; failed=all takes rejected (should carry a fallback_asset_type or manual follow-up).

shot.$comment: JSON Schema's regex flavor (ECMA-262) has no reliable inline case-insensitive/word-boundary shorthand across all validators, so this schema-level if/then only catches literal digits in script_line as a conservative baseline. validate_shotlist.py implements the fuller rule from the spec ('contains a factual number' also covers percent/cents/dollar signs and spelled-out number-words like two-thirds, half, dozen, nickel, dime) and additionally warns — rather than errors — when a number appears only in on_screen (e.g. a CARD or chart label) rather than in script_line, since doc 17 places some [VERIFY] figures there (see shot 7's on-screen '~$2B, 3-5 years' capex card, spoken script_line has no digit).
